title: Two Queens, One Throne Room
setting: A presence chamber furnished from two centuries at once - Tudor panelling, Hellenistic couches, a single chair of state that neither woman is willing to be the second to sit in. Their households have been left outside.
stakes: Which strategy for a woman holding a throne alone actually survives contact with men and with time.

roles_in_scene.elizabeth-i: Queen of England, who has kept power for thirty years by never concluding a negotiation
roles_in_scene.cleopatra: Pharaoh of Egypt, who kept a kingdom alive by attaching it to the strongest Roman available

opening_line: Two women who ruled alone, in a room with one chair.
